headline: Microsoft launches AI transparency initiative with 40 partners
dek: Open standards for AI agents are the goal, per Microsoft.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The launch
body: Microsoft announced the AI Transparency Initiative at Ignite, unveiled by Satya Nadella, per Microsoft Source.
The aim is an open security and governance standard for AI models and agents (Microsoft Source).

points.t: More AI autonomy requires more transparency.
Teams see around the model, not inside it.
Agents act without human approval at each step.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Who is in
body: The company says it works with more than 40 partners, including Accenture, Adobe, KPMG, Mastercard and Volvo Cars (Microsoft Source).
It is also expanding its role in a NIST standards initiative (Microsoft Source).

items.t: Microsoft AI, Foundry and Copilot will build it in.
They can use the evidence in their own tools.
The company gave no availability date.

caption.hook: Microsoft launched the AI Transparency Initiative to build open security standards for AI agents.
body: Per Microsoft Source, Satya Nadella made the announcement at Ignite. The company sums up the principle in one line: greater AI autonomy requires greater transparency. Today, it says, organizations can watch the activity around a model but cannot see what happens inside it.

Microsoft says it works with more than 40 partners, such as Accenture, Adobe, KPMG, Mastercard and Volvo Cars, and is expanding its role in a NIST standards initiative. The work will be built into Microsoft AI, Foundry and Copilot, but the company gave no timeline for availability.
caption.cta: Should every AI agent be verifiable from the inside?
